transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

My family says I’m always getting sidetracked and forgetting what I was supposed to be doing, and they were starting to worry it might be some kind of early memory decline. After I missed another appointment recently, my primary care doctor suggested I get evaluated to look into these long-standing difficulties with staying mentally on track.
Have you struggled with getting sidetracked and forgetting things since you were a child, or is this a relatively recent change?

These problems have gotten much more noticeable over the past year since I retired and took on more responsibilities, but they actually go all the way back to my childhood. Even back in primary school, my teachers would complain to my parents that I was always daydreaming, missing instructions, and forgetting to bring home the right books.
Since retiring and noticing these difficulties getting worse over the past year, have you also been feeling down, depressed, or losing interest in activities you normally enjoy?

No, I don't feel depressed or lose interest in my activities at all. I actually really enjoy my hobbies and volunteering at the senior center, but the main issue is that I get sidetracked and have a hard time staying organized with everything. It's more about managing all the tasks rather than not wanting to do them.
Over the past year, have you experienced any new medical conditions, head injuries, or significant changes in your physical health?
No, I haven't had any head injuries, new medical conditions, or any major changes like that over the past year. My physical health has actually been generally stable and fine.
Along with these difficulties focusing, do you often feel physically restless, have trouble sitting still, or find yourself acting impulsively?

Yes, I do feel quite restless inside, especially during long meetings or in waiting rooms where I keep shifting in my seat and looking for an excuse to stand up. I also have a hard time with quiet activities like reading or meditation because my legs get fidgety and my mind wanders. Usually, I just end up getting up to tinker with something instead.
Do you also find yourself frequently interrupting others during conversations, blurting out answers before a question is finished, or having a hard time waiting your turn?
No, I don't think I have those specific difficulties. I generally don't interrupt others, blurt out answers, or have trouble waiting my turn during conversations.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a lifelong history of inattention (getting sidetracked, forgetfulness, disorganization, daydreaming, and missing instructions) and hyperactivity (internal restlessness, difficulty remaining seated, fidgeting during quiet activities) dating back to childhood (primary school). These symptoms cause significant functional impairment in managing daily responsibilities and appointments, and are not better explained by a mood disorder, medical condition, or head injury, meeting the criteria for Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ICD-10 F90.0).
